# Function to parse coolors.co URL for hex codes (2025-11-12 01:35Z)

_**User (2025-11-13 01:27Z)**_

I need a function, `convertCoolorToArray` that will intake a coolors.co url, parse it, and return an array of {name, color} objects. The name and the color properties will be the hashtag-prefixed hex-codes extracted from the url. The urls look like this `https://coolors.co/palette/780000-c1121f-fdf0d5-003049-669bbc` with an arbitrary (>1) number of hex colors separated by hyphens.

  { name: 'foo', color: '#676767' },
  { name: 'foo', color: '#808080' },
  { name: 'foo', color: '#ffffff' },
  { name: 'foo', color: '#f5f5f5' },
  { name: 'foo', color: '#e2e5de' },
  { name: 'foo', color: '#b2beb5' }
]

const convertCoolorToArray = (coolor) => {
  // Example: https://coolors.co/palette/780000-c1121f-fdf0d5-003049-669bbc
  // Extract the last part after the last slash
  const lastSlash = coolor.lastIndexOf('/')
  if (lastSlash === -1) return []
  const palettePart = coolor.substring(lastSlash + 1)
  // Remove 'palette/' if present
  const palette = palettePart.replace(/^palette\//, '')
  // Split by hyphen
  const hexes = palette.split('-')
  // Only allow valid 3 or 6 digit hex codes
  return hexes
    .filter(h => /^[0-9a-fA-F]{3,6}$/.test(h))
    .map(h => {
      const hex = '#' + h.toLowerCase()
      return { name: hex, color: hex }
    })
}

_**User (2025-11-13 05:00Z)**_

With ES modules, what are the best way for me to export the array of pallettes so I don't have to concatenate into an array on import?

---

_**Agent (model copilot/gpt-4.1)**_

With ES modules, the best way to export multiple palettes so you can import them as a single array without manual concatenation is to export them individually and also export a combined array. For example:

```javascript
export const PALETTE = [/* ... */]
export const PALETTE_TWO = [/* ... */]
export const BONE_WHITE = [/* ... */]

// Export all palettes as a single array
export const ALL_PALETTES = [PALETTE, PALETTE_TWO, BONE_WHITE]
```

Then, in your import:

```javascript
import { ALL_PALETTES } from './risocolors.js'
// ALL_PALETTES is already a combined array of all palettes
```

This approach is clean, avoids manual concatenation on import, and keeps your exports organized.
